title: Hold an IV bag still on a slick tray while the other hand uncaps its port, spikes it and primes the drip chamber
instruction: Get the IV bag ready for an infusion: hold the bag still on the tray by its hanger tab with one hand, and with the other pull the blue cap off its spike port, push the giving set's spike into the port all the way until it locks, then squeeze the drip chamber twice so it fills about halfway. Then let go of both and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Spiking an IV bag and priming the drip chamber is a routine nursing step before every infusion; the soft bag has to be held while the spike is driven firmly into its port.
setup: Station table, one fixed layout. A smooth stainless-steel tray (34 x 54 cm, 4 mm) covers the middle of the table. On it lies a 500 ml PVC bag of saline (10 x 15 cm, 2.2 cm thick, 500 g, welded rim, white printed label) at x 0.32, y 0.06 m, a stiff PVC hanger tab (28 x 8 x 20 mm) folded up on its far end, toward the left arm, and its two ports toward the right arm: a white spike port (10 mm across, 3 cm long) closed by a blue polyethylene pull-off cap with a tab, and a medication port beside it. To the right lies an infusion giving set: a white polycarbonate spike (25 mm) on a clear PVC drip chamber (20 mm across, 4.5 cm long, marks at a third and two thirds), a 10 cm stub of clear tubing and a blue roller clamp, the spike pointing toward the bag, the chamber's middle at x 0.42, y -0.13 m. The bag slides on the tray at a light push (about 0.25 N).
scoring: 1.0: the spike locked all the way into the port (its collar on the port's mouth), the drip chamber a third to two thirds full (one or two squeezes, counted only after the spike locked: each squeeze, let go, draws in a third), the bag still on the tray and both hands let go (each TCP at least 4 cm from the drip chamber and the port's mouth), and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start). 0.5: the spike locked in the port. 0.25: the cap pulled off. 0.0 otherwise. The spike can only go in once the cap is off, and once locked stays locked. The trial ends early once the full score has held for 1 s with the bag and the giving set still.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The bag is a rigid pillow on a low-friction tray. The cap is held on by a joint that breaks at 3.5 N. The spike in the port is a sliding joint switched on when the spike's tip enters the port in line, held by a stick-slip grip of about 1.5 N and locked at full depth. The saline is not a fluid: each squeeze of the drip chamber (fingers closed on it, then opened) shows another third of a chamber of saline.
